title: Completely monotone negative powers of hyperbolic polynomials
body_text:
Completely monotone negative powers of hyperbolic polynomials

Scott and Sokal asked whether every homogeneous polynomial with the half-plane property has a completely monotone negative power. We show that it does, and prove the positivity conjectures of Michałek--Sturmfels--Uhler--Zwiernik and Kozhasov--Michałek--Sturmfels. For a homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial in $n\ge2$ variables, positive on its hyperbolicity cone, every power $p^{-α}$ with $α\ge4096n^2$ is completely monotone, independently of the degree and coefficients of $p$. When the cone has pointed closure, its Riesz kernel is strictly log-concave in the interior of the dual cone, with relative Gaussian comparison error at most $512n^2/α$ and explicit Hessian bounds. We also prove that positive exponents of complete monotonicity can accumulate at zero only if $p$ is a product of real linear forms. The specialized V'amos quartic provides an example with no definite determinantal representation of any positive integer power.

Authors: Dongsheng Wei
Categories: math.CO, math.AG, math.CA, math.CO
